stories.title: Lindsay Clancy's family was 'very concerned' about her mental health in the months before she killed her kids
stories.summary:
Lindsay Clancy's family expressed deep concern about her mental health in the months leading up to the deaths of her three children. Her mother-in-law testified that Clancy was "begging for help" with severe insomnia and anxiety before the Duxbury killings.

Clancy has admitted to killing her daughter and two sons but has pleaded not guilty to murder. She stated she was experiencing postpartum psychosis at the time of the incidents.

stories.title: UK 'supports Ukraine 100%', Burnham says, after Russia's drone warning
stories.summary:
UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer has reaffirmed Britain's full support for Ukraine following a warning from Moscow over the supply of British-made drones. Russia accused the UK of escalating the conflict by providing these weapons, framing the move as an intensification of the war rather than defensive assistance.

Despite the Russian criticism, Starmer stated that the UK supports Ukraine 100% and pledged to stand with Kyiv during its "hour of need." The comments highlight a growing diplomatic tension over Western military aid, with Moscow viewing drone deliveries as a direct step toward deeper involvement in the conflict.

Committee officials stated that Bragg's approach has led to an increase in violent crime and created dangerous conditions for residents. The hearing is titled "Victims of Violent Crime in Manhattan."

The event highlights the committee's current legislative priorities regarding public safety and local law enforcement strategies.

stories.title: Talarico campaign poaches former Cornyn staffer in race against Paxton
stories.summary:
Jacob Smith, a former senior aide to outgoing Texas Sen. John Cornyn, has joined the U.S. Senate campaign of Democratic state Sen. James Talarico. The move marks an unexpected cross-party shift in the high-stakes race against Republican nominee Ken Paxton.

Smith previously served as Cornyn’s deputy legislative director and policy adviser for five years. He is now working as Talarico’s deputy policy director, bringing significant experience to the Democratic effort.

The defection has drawn attention from multiple news outlets, including Breitbart, Fox News, and The Washington Examiner. As the Texas Senate battle heats up, Smith's transition underscores the competitive nature of a race that could influence Republican control of the chamber.

stories.title: Dickovers, baggravation and botiquette: 18 new words to describe our tech hellscape
stories.summary:
The Guardian has compiled a list of 18 new words intended to describe common digital annoyances, arguing that modern technology creates specific irritants for which the English language previously lacked precise vocabulary.

A central example is the “dickover,” a term coined in May by tech writer John Gruber. It refers to modal panels or popovers that deliberately obscure content to frustrate users, forcing them to click away from unwanted elements before accessing their intended destination.

The article frames these linguistic additions as a response to what it calls a “tech hellscape,” providing terminology for the various ways digital interfaces can obstruct user experience.

Coined in May by John Gruber, a tech writer, it is defined as “a modal panel, popover, or curtain presented by a website or app, deliberately obscuring its own content to frustrate the user”. stories.title: Democracy v the machine: the birth of the digital age and the warnings that were ignored
stories.summary:
The Guardian examines the early history of the digital age and the warnings that were ignored as technology advanced. The article argues that while many hoped technological progress would create an egalitarian utopia, some observers foresaw threats to liberal society.

The piece notes a current cultural fixation on future possibilities, including the future of work, humanity, and the planet. It suggests this forward-looking anxiety has obscured the historical context of how digital technology developed and the concerns raised during its emergence.

Classes were suspended across several regions of the Philippines on Wednesday, August 19, due to bad weather brought by the southwest monsoon. The suspensions affected areas including Pampanga, Batangas, Cavite, Mimaropa, Oriental Mindoro, Ilocos Region, Metro Manila, and Cordillera.

In Batangas, five local governments extended the suspension of face-to-face classes at all levels to Wednesday. These included Batangas City and the municipalities of Calaca City, Bauan, Lobo, and Tingloy.

The decision was made in response to heavy rains that continued to impact their communities.

In addition to adjusting work schedules for public employees, the order includes provisions for education. Unless local chief executives issue different instructions, schools at all levels are expected to implement alternative learning modes and continuity measures.

stories.title: ‘The kids were right’: 30 years of Pokémon, from school-wide bans to multimillion-dollar trading cards
stories.summary:
Pokémon has marked 30 years of cultural presence, outlasting the early moral panics that once led to school-wide bans in Australia. The franchise’s longevity suggests its appeal was built on simple joy rather than fleeting trend.

For many Australians, the show became a morning ritual, often watched before school as part of curated cartoon blocks like Cheez TV. That childhood exposure helped establish a fan base that has persisted for decades.

Today, Pokémon extends far beyond television into collectibles, with trading cards now reaching multimillion-dollar values at auction. The franchise’s evolution reflects how early skepticism gave way to mainstream acceptance and commercial success.

stories.title: Claude to start watermarking AI-generated text – but will it make quality worse?
stories.summary:
Anthropic says Claude will begin watermarking AI-generated text as part of its effort to comply with EU regulation. The company plans to change the way the chatbot makes small, random choices when producing output.

The move has raised questions about whether the new approach could degrade writing quality. Readers and commentators have already noted common patterns in machine-generated prose, including overuse of the word “delve,” excess em dashes, and repetitive constructions such as “it’s not X but Y.” The Guardian frames the issue as a potential trade-off between regulatory compliance and the naturalness of Claude’s text.

stories.summary:
Dressmaker is a design game co-created by developer Jonathan Hau-Yoon and his sewing-obsessed partner, Sabrina Becker. The project was inspired by Hau-Yoon’s desire to make something as meaningful as the environmental strategy game Terra Nil.

Becker had worn a dress she made herself to an event, which sparked the concept for the game. According to its lead programmer, Dressmaker has been “the most technically challenging” project he has ever worked on.
